title: Jump and Jump
statement:
You are initially at point P on a number line.

You have to make exactly X jumps, where each jump has a length of L.

For every jump, you can move either:
- Forward by L
- Backward by L

Your task is to find and return the minimum possible absolute value of the final position after performing exactly X jumps.

Input Format:
- input1: An integer P, representing the initial position.
- input2: An integer X, representing the number of jumps.
- input3: An integer L, representing the length of each jump.

Output Format:
- Print a single integer representing the minimum possible absolute value of the final position.

examples.explanation:
Initial P = 7, X = 4 jumps of L = 3.
If we make 3 backward jumps (-9) and 1 forward jump (+3), net movement = -6.
Final position = 7 - 6 = 1.
Absolute value = |1| = 1.

Initial P = 10, X = 2 jumps of L = 5.
Two backward jumps (-10) gives net movement = -10.
Final position = 10 - 10 = 0.
Absolute value = |0| = 0.

Initial P = 5, X = 3 jumps of L = 2.
3 backward jumps (-6) gives final position = 5 - 6 = -1.
Absolute value = |-1| = 1.

hints: If k jumps are forward and (X - k) jumps are backward, the net movement is (2*k - X) * L.
The final position is P + (2*k - X) * L for some 0 <= k <= X.
Iterate k from 0 to X and track the minimum absolute value |P + (2*k - X) * L|.
discussion: Single parameter search or math clamping to find minimum absolute distance after X jumps.
